Brent is $88.91 (+3.24%, Yahoo Finance, Aug 31), WTI is $86.64 (+3.89%, Yahoo Finance, Aug 31), and TTF is 66.56 EUR/MWh (-0.63%, Yahoo Finance, Aug 28). Crisis level remains 4 (High); base 10%, stress 60%, tail 30%.

todaysEvents.delta: The Aug 25 Oman-Iran statement keeps a proposed temporary corridor and mine-clearance project in technical negotiation; Aug 27 reporting described revenue sharing, but Iran's reopening conditions remain unmet (Oman FM/Al Jazeera, Aug 25-27).

Qatar's prime minister met Iran's foreign minister in Tehran on Aug 27 to discuss de-escalation and the proposed Hormuz corridor; no signed reopening or cleared commercial lane has been verified (Al Jazeera, Aug 27).
Yahoo Finance shows Brent at $88.91 (+3.24%) and WTI at $86.64 (+3.89%) on Aug 31; TTF was 66.56 EUR/MWh (-0.63%) on Aug 28, keeping energy volatility elevated.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and Oman advance a temporary corridor and mine-clearance framework; a signed, monitored reopening restores traffic and lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The corridor remains provisional and traffic stays selective under Iranian fees, sanctions pressure and residual mine and attack risk; Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated while Qatar's force majeure runs through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: A failed framework, further tanker attack or sanctions retaliation could close the southern lane again and spill into Bab el-Mandeb; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.

priceNarratives.Brent: Pre-shock ~$65 -> $126 wartime high intraday (Day 59, Apr 30, CNBC/CNN) -> $88.91 (Aug 31, Yahoo Finance BZ=F; +3.24%) as the conditional Iran-Oman corridor framework met continued reopening and sanctions uncertainty. Working range $75-85 base (signed workable deal); $78-95 stress (conditional routing); $105-135+ tail (renewed closure).
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Reuters September-delivery assessment) as sustained Hormuz disruption tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $23.18/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Aug 28), down 1.0%. Qatar force majeure is carried through mid-September from the Reuters Jul 23 notice; the reported mid-October extension remains unconfirmed.
priceNarratives.TTF Gas: Pre-shock ~$34/MWh -> 63.58/MWh (Jul 24, MacroMicro) -> 66.56 EUR/MWh (Aug 28, Yahoo Finance TTF=F; -0.63%) as Iran-Oman corridor diplomacy remained conditional and Qatar LNG force majeure persisted. The marker remains elevated versus the pre-crisis baseline while route and supply risks remain unresolved.
priceNarratives.Credit: iTraxx Asia IG est. ~138bp (Aug 5, -2bp); ASEAN HY est. ~475bp (-8bp), both carried pending fresher EM credit data.
